intro: Property managers choose tenants by applying a consistent, written set of qualification criteria to every applicant. This process relies on objective metrics like credit scores and rent to income ratios rather than subjective judgment.

blocks.text: Why standardized screening matters for your portfolio

When you ask how do property managers choose tenants, the answer should always be through a structured, repeatable process. Inconsistency is your biggest risk. If you apply different rules to different people, you open your business to Fair Housing complaints. These legal battles are costly and time consuming.

Beyond legal risks, there is the financial reality of bad debt. Screened tenants are 1.2 times more likely to pay rent on time. When you lack a standard, you might skip a step like calling a previous landlord or verifying a pay stub. That small shortcut can lead to an eviction, which costs between $3,500 and $10,000 per case.
The rise of rental application fraud

Rental application fraud is increasing. Over 93 percent of managers report seeing fake pay stubs or manipulated bank statements. This represents a 40 percent year over year increase. Nearly 24 percent of all eviction filings are linked to tenants who submitted fraudulent applications.

If you rely on manual document review without a system, you are vulnerable. You need a process that verifies data at the source. Automated bank integrations are harder to fake than a PDF bank statement.
How to build a standardized screening workflow

items: Create a written document outlining your qualification criteria.
Include specific thresholds for credit scores and rent to income ratios.
Apply these rules to every applicant without exception.
Use property management software to keep an audit trail of every decision.
Implement a waterfall verification process starting with automated data.

blocks.text: Your software should act as the single source of truth. Whether you use AppFolio, Buildium, or DoorLoop, ensure all documents are uploaded to the platform. Do not keep applicant data in your email inbox. If you need to share a file, use the secure portals provided by your software.
Managing your screening process on a Mac

Most modern property management tools run in a browser. Whether you prefer Safari, Chrome, or Firefox, your Mac is perfectly capable of handling these tasks. The key is to keep your browser updated. Security patches are vital when you handle sensitive tenant data.

Use macOS Preview to review signed leases or documents. If you receive a PDF that needs a signature, open it in Preview. Use the Markup toolbar to add your signature. This keeps the document flow within your local system until you are ready to upload it back to your management platform.
Always follow your employer guidelines when handling sensitive applicant data. Do not store personal identification information on your local desktop if your company policy forbids it.

blocks.text: What to do when you suspect fraud

If a document looks suspicious, do not guess. Ask the applicant to provide a direct link to their bank account using a secure integration tool. If they refuse, you have your answer. Standardized procedures make it easier to say no without feeling like you are being unfair.

faq.question: What is the most important part of screening?
faq.answer: Consistency. Having a written, objective policy that you apply to every single applicant is the best way to avoid legal issues and ensure you are choosing reliable tenants.

faq.question: How do I spot fake bank statements?
faq.answer: Look for inconsistencies in font, alignment, or transaction history. The best defense is to use integrated screening tools that pull data directly from the applicant's bank account.

faq.question: Do I need special software for my Mac?
faq.answer: No. Most property management software is cloud based. You only need a modern web browser like Safari or Chrome to access your dashboard and manage your applicants.

costs.title: Legal liability
costs.text: Inconsistent screening often leads to Fair Housing violations, which carry heavy fines and legal fees.

costs.title: Eviction expenses
costs.text: A single eviction can cost you between $3,500 and $10,000 in legal and turnover costs.

costs.title: Time loss
costs.text: Manual data entry and repeated follow ups with applicants for missing documents drain hours of your week.

causes.title: Lack of written criteria
causes.text: Without a clear, documented policy, managers often make decisions based on gut feeling or incomplete information.

causes.title: Siloed data
causes.text: Keeping application details in emails and PDFs instead of a central platform makes it easy to miss red flags.

causes.title: Manual verification
causes.text: Relying on physical documents that can be easily manipulated makes it harder to catch professional rental fraud.

fixes.title: Define your standards
fixes.text: Create a written document with your credit score and income requirements. Use this for every applicant.

fixes.title: Automate verification
fixes.text: Use tools that connect directly to bank accounts or payroll providers to verify income and assets.

fixes.title: Centralize all data
fixes.text: Move all application communication and documents into your property management software to maintain a clear audit trail.
